assets.name: Gold

assets.name: US 10-year Treasury yield
assets.what: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years. It sets the tone for mortgage rates and for how much investors pay for stocks.

context.label: US 10-year Treasury yield, Nov 25, 2026
context.detail: The yield fell nearly 12 basis points to 4.81% on Nov 25, its lowest since September, as investors bought Treasuries for safety during the AI stock selloff and digested new tariff proposals. That came even as core PCE inflation rose to 3.3% and growth was revised up, data that markets read as keeping a December Fed hike on track.

assets.what: What a typical buyer pays on a 30-year fixed loan. It follows the 10-year Treasury yield plus a spread for risk and lender costs.

context.detail: The average 30-year rate eased to 7.21% from 7.28% a week earlier, and the 15-year to 6.54% from 6.66%, following the drop in Treasury yields. A year ago the 30-year averaged 6.23%.

assets.name: US dollar index
assets.what: Measures the dollar against the euro, yen, pound and others. A stronger dollar makes imports cheaper for Americans and dollar debts heavier for other countries.

context.label: US dollar index, Nov 25, 2026
context.detail: The dollar climbed to its highest level since April 2025 in mid-November as Fed officials signaled more rate hikes to fight inflation. Higher US rates attract money into dollars, and safe-haven buying during the stock selloff and new tariffs added support.

context.detail: National home prices rose 2.1% from a year earlier, the same as in August, while consumer prices rose 3.7%. That makes September the 16th straight month in which home prices fell after inflation; Chicago led at +6.9% and Seattle fell most at -1.9%.
